reason: Native <textarea> styling plus one piece of registry-layer state: a use_signal-tracked character count that renders the `N / max` counter when `max_length` is set. The count mirrors the native input's own value length rather than owning any editing behavior, so no existing primitive (use_controlled is for controlled/uncontrolled value ownership, which stays with the consumer here) is a natural owner.
followUp: If a second registry item needs the same typed-length-tracking shape (e.g. a counter on input or input-group), promote it into a small shared primitive instead of duplicating the count-mirroring signal at the registry layer again.
